title: Stuck on what to do financially, would like advice
body:
O.P.
Hi all,
I'd love to get some input on what I should do in regards to my finances as I feel like I've indecisive for way too long and if I keep this up I'll just hurt myself financially even further.
So for context, one of my main goals in life is to own my own house to live in.
I'm 33yo and make a bit over 70k/yr I currently have ~150k total sitting liquid in my bank accounts, 40k of that is not in a HISA account which I really should setup a new account at a different bank for.
I've was told if I plan on buying a property soon I should not invest it into the market so I kept saving for a deposit. It's been 5 years since then and I still haven't gotten a place so I'm re-evaluating if I should just forgo getting a place and just dump the excess 40k into the market along with the existing ~50k i have in ETFs and just DCA into there instead?
I've been neglecting my super, just having my employer put in the legally required amount in there so it's about 50k in there. Looking at the super thread in this form, lots of people in their 30s have high 6 figure amounts which makes me worry i'm very far behind.
Another thing is I've been looking at possibly purchasing a "new" car as my current on is 18 years old now and has lots of sun damage/rust on the roof which would cost more to repair than the value of the car itself. So i'm thinking of just getting a new car and trade in the current one for whatever value i can get for it.
I'm tempted to go for a used Subaru BRZ which I know isn't the most financially smartest move but I think we're getting to a point where ICE vehicles are starting to slowly get phased out and I'd like to own one sporty car in my life so this is more of an personal desire than anything. Otherwise sure I could just go for some cheap, reliable japanese sedan. I'd be daily driving it mostly to and from work, I only do about 5000-10,000km at most per year
So TD;DR , Should I forgo saving for a home and just go all in on ETFs with DCA and start contributing more to my super? Also should I get a BRZ to satisfy one of my personal bucketlist items or just do the smart thing and get a cheap, reliable car instead to daily?
Thanks for any advice, suggestions in advance!

[User #3000433243 postsPierre2Whirlpool Forums Addict] you really do need 15 – 20 % deposit for any house, and don't have anywhere near enough for that – or even 10% deposit.
maybe goto some more EFTs instead, or dump the lot into Your Super, But, you could have issues in getting that back, earlier – if needed . . what about some blue-chip shares ?. - any car is always an loss maker, unfortunately, even when you do need one.
it's that time of the year, too, maybe Talk to Your Accountant, instead ?.
[User #7964355185 postsbm123Whirlpool Forums Addict] If your main goal is to buy a property to live in then determine at what price point, how much you need to save for a deposit, how long will that take you. If under 10 years then don’t invest in equities (shares) through ETF’s, stick with HISA’s. Can you invest in yourself to increase your income?
You had a similar thread with good advice that is still applicable a few years ago: /thread/96p2q519
[User #4703112089 postscoffee44Whirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
If you can buy a place, buy a place and never have to move again in your lifetime. We are only going to jam more and more people into Australia over the next 30 years, so i'm fairly confident that prices are not going to go down and only go one way over the next 10-30 years. Once you have a place you can sort out the other things, Super/Shares/Car etc
I use the KISS principle (keep it simple stupid)
BTW, which city are you in and have you seen a mortgage broker or bank to see how much you can borrow. Can you use the governments 5% deposit scheme for housing.

I'm 33yo and make a bit over 70k/yr I currently have ~150k total You are young and not in Sydney (most expensive city in Australia), so with government’s scheme of 5% deposit and government paying the rest, you should be able to buy a property. Don’t wait for saving a 20% deposit as you will be waiting forever. Get a house first, super, ETFs can wait. Your main problem is not a small deposit, but a low salary. Buy a house and then invest in yourself (skills, education) and boost your income so that you can save more. Otherwise, team up with someone (eg partner) to buy a house as a couple.

[User #5200781 postsDavid McPaulWhirlpool Enthusiast] Not advice but here are some thoughts.
1. Thinking Unit instead of House might be a better path. 2. You can put money into Super and access it to buy your first home (up to $50000) See https://propertywithsuperannu ation.com/accessing-super-for-house-deposit/ This might be a good place to park some money while you think and grow your super. 3. 150K is a 20% deposit on a 750K property. I would not try for that but a quick search seems to show plenty of 2 bedroom units under $700K. I don't know the Perth market so not idea what is a good deal there. 4. Borrowing 550-600 on a 70K salary is too much I think but maybe with a partner or friend? 5. Set some goals. Maybe work towards only needing to borrow 450 so another 100K. How long did it take to get 150K
[User #8576154406 postsMMXXVIWhirlpool Forums Addict] You also should focus on increasing your income as well.
I know a lot of friends in their 20s earning >$100k so maybe upskill or do something else that could earn you more for someone your age, unless there’s something preventing you from doing that.
